candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: apply infection-prevention practices, handle contaminated materials safely, and prevent environmental transmission of infectious agents.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — contaminated-linen handling
candidate.educational_objective: Handle contaminated healthcare linen with minimum agitation, contain it at the point of use, avoid sorting or prerinsing it in patient-care areas, and use leak-resistant containment when indicated.

options.A: Sort contaminated linen in the client room before bagging so heavily soiled pieces can be separated early.
options.B: Handle the linen with minimum agitation and contain it at the point of use, using leak-resistant containment when blood or body substances could soak through.
options.C: Shake contaminated linen before bagging to remove loose material and reduce the laundry load.
options.D: Prerinse contaminated linen in the patient-care area before placing it in the transport container.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC environmental infection-control recommendations direct healthcare personnel to handle contaminated textiles with minimum agitation, bag or otherwise contain them at the point of use, avoid sorting or prerinsing them in patient-care areas, and use leak-resistant containment for textiles contaminated with blood or body substances when leakage or soak-through is possible. Therefore B is correct. A and D perform prohibited sorting/prerinsing in the care area, while C increases agitation and potential aerosolization/dispersion of contaminated material.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Contaminated linen should be minimally agitated and contained at the point of use, not sorted or prerininsed in patient-care areas, with leak-resistant containment when blood/body-fluid contamination can leak or soak through.
candidate.source_document_title: Part II. Recommendations for Environmental Infection Control in Health-Care Facilities; Laundry and Bedding
candidate.source_locator: Laundry and Bedding > G.III Routine Handling of Contaminated Laundry: minimum agitation; contain at point of use; do not sort or prerinse in patient-care areas; use leak-resistant containment for blood/body-substance contamination. Laundry and Bedding > Collecting, Transporting, and Sorting reiterates the same principles.
